candidates.comment: A textual representation of the telephone number for a contact point, organization, person, or place. Also called "phone number", "contact number", "telecom number". Examples: "The organization has telephone +1-555-123-4567", "The person's telephone is 555-987-6543", "The place lists its telephone number."

candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer
candidates.comment: A participation offer relation between an event and an offer to participate in it. Also called call for participation, participation opportunity, event entry offer. Examples: "An event has a participation offer for speakers.", "The conference has a participation offer for proposals.", "This festival includes a participation offer for performers.". Distinct from hasSponsorshipOffer, which is an offer to sponsor the event.

relations.definition: The subject entity proposed assistance to the object entity.
relations.embedding_query_text: offered to help: The subject entity proposed assistance to the object entity.

chosen_property.label: offeredHelpTo
chosen_property.definition: The subject entity proposed assistance to the object entity.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits this relation.

candidates.label: lender
candidates.comment: A lending participant relation between a borrow action and the person or organization providing the object being borrowed. Also called: loan provider, creditor, financing entity. Examples: "BorrowAction lender Bank of America", "BorrowAction lender John Doe", "BorrowAction lender Library".

candidates.label: itemOffered
candidates.comment: A transaction subject relation between a demand or offer and the specific item, product, service, or event being requested or provided. Also called offered item, demanded item, subject of offer, product/service offered. Examples: An offer has an itemOffered of 'a new car'. A demand has an itemOffered of 'web design service'. An offer has an itemOffered of 'a concert ticket'. Distinct from itemReviewed, which is the subject of a review, not an offer/demand.

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: funding
candidates.comment: A funding relation between a biochemical entity, creative work, event, medical entity, organization, person, or product and the grant that provides its direct or indirect financial support. Also called: grant received, sponsorship, financial support. Examples: "Cancer Research Project" funding "NIH Grant R01", "Local Theater Production" funding "Arts Council Grant", "Student Scholarship Program" funding "University Endowment Grant". Distinct from funder, which is the entity providing the funding.

candidates.label: itemReviewed
candidates.comment: A review subject relation between an aggregate rating or review and the entity that is being evaluated or rated. Also called reviewed item, rated item, subject of review, evaluated entity. Examples: A review has an itemReviewed of 'Restaurant X'. An aggregate rating has an itemReviewed of 'Movie Y'. A product review has an itemReviewed of 'Smartphone Z'. Distinct from itemOffered, which is the subject of an offer or demand.

candidates.label: observationAbout
candidates.comment: An entity, often a place, that an observation is about or associated with. Also called observed entity, subject of observation, related to observation. Examples: "Weather Observation observationAbout 'London'", "Patient Vitals Observation observationAbout 'John Doe'", "Traffic Count Observation observationAbout 'Main Street'".

candidates.label: softwareHelp
candidates.comment: A relation between a software application and a creative work providing assistance or guidance for its use. Also called "application help", "software documentation", "user guide for software". Examples: "Microsoft Word has softwareHelp a user manual", "The app's softwareHelp is an online FAQ", "This softwareHelp explains how to use the program."

candidates.label: fundedItem
candidates.comment: A funded item relation between a grant and the biochemical entity, creative work, event, medical entity, organization, person, or product that receives direct or indirect funding or sponsorship. Also called: grant recipient, sponsored item, supported entity. Examples: "Research Grant" funded item "Cancer Research Project", "Arts Grant" funded item "Local Theater Production", "Educational Grant" funded item "Student Scholarship Program". Distinct from funding, which is the grant itself.

candidates.label: offeredBy
candidates.comment: An organization or person making an offer. Also called provided by, seller, vendor, offered from. Examples: "Product Offer offeredBy 'Acme Corp'", "Service Offer offeredBy 'John Doe'", "Event Ticket Offer offeredBy 'Ticketmaster'". Distinct from seller, which is a more specific term for a person or organization selling something.

candidates.label: offers
candidates.comment: An offer or demand related to a product, service, event, or other item. Also called available offers, related offers, product offers. Examples: "Product X offers 'Offer to sell'", "Service Y offers 'Demand for service'", "Event Z offers 'Offer for tickets'". Distinct from hasOfferCatalog, which points to a catalog of offers.

chosen_property.label: spokeWith
chosen_property.definition: The subject entity had a conversation with the object entity.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits this relation.

candidates.label: spokenByCharacter
candidates.comment: An attribution relation between a quotation and the character, person, or organization to whom it is attributed within a creative work. Also called "attributed to", "quote speaker", "character says", "uttered by". Examples: "The quote is spokenByCharacter Hamlet", "The dialogue was spokenByCharacter the CEO", "This line is spokenByCharacter a fictional narrator."

candidates.label: knowsLanguage
candidates.comment: A language proficiency relation between an organization or person and a language they are able to communicate in. Also called speaks language, fluent in, understands language, conversant in. Examples: A person knowsLanguage 'English'. An organization knowsLanguage 'Spanish'. A diplomat knowsLanguage 'French' (fr).

candidates.label: knows
candidates.comment: A general acquaintance relation between two people who are known to each other socially or professionally. Also called acquainted with, familiar with, knows personally, has met. Examples: John knows 'Jane'. Sarah knows 'her colleague Tom'. The CEO knows 'the board members'. Distinct from follows, friend, or memberOf, which imply more specific types of relationships.

candidates.label: language
candidates.comment: A communication medium relation between a communicate action or write action and the language employed in that action. Also called language used, medium of communication, spoken in, written in. Examples: A communicate action uses the language 'English'. A write action uses the language 'French'. A conversation has the language 'Spanish'. Distinct from inLanguage, which is for the language of a creative work itself, not the action of communicating/writing.

candidates.label: transcript
candidates.comment: A transcript relation between an audio or video object and the text of its spoken content. Also called audio text, video text, spoken content. Examples: "AudioObject transcript 'Hello, welcome to the podcast.'", "VideoObject transcript 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.'", "Lecture recording transcript 'Today we will discuss quantum physics.'".

candidates.label: connectedTo
candidates.comment: A connection relation between an anatomical structure and other anatomical structures it is connected to. Also called "linked to", "adjoins", "connects with". Examples: "Femur anatomical structure connectedTo Tibia", "Brain anatomical structure connectedTo Spinal cord".

candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer
candidates.comment: A participation offer relation between an event and an offer to participate in it. Also called call for participation, participation opportunity, event entry offer. Examples: "An event has a participation offer for speakers.", "The conference has a participation offer for proposals.", "This festival includes a participation offer for performers.". Distinct from hasSponsorshipOffer, which is an offer to sponsor the event.

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

chosen_property.label: used
chosen_property.definition: The subject entity utilized the object entity.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits this relation.

candidates.label: usedToDiagnose
candidates.comment: A used to diagnose relation between a medical test and a medical condition it is employed to identify. Also called diagnoses, identifies condition, screens for. Examples: "MedicalTest 'MRI' usedToDiagnose 'Brain Tumor'", "MedicalTest 'Blood Test' usedToDiagnose 'Anemia'", "MedicalTest 'X-ray' usedToDiagnose 'Fracture'".

candidates.label: usesDevice
candidates.comment: A uses device relation between a medical test and the medical device employed to perform it. Also called device used, equipment for test, test instrument. Examples: "MedicalTest 'Ultrasound' usesDevice 'Ultrasound Scanner'", "MedicalTest 'ECG' usesDevice 'Electrocardiograph'", "MedicalTest 'Blood Pressure Measurement' usesDevice 'Sphygmomanometer'".

candidates.label: recipe
candidates.comment: A recipe relation between a cook action and the specific recipe used as an instrument. Also called recipe used, instructions for, cooking guide. Examples: "A cook action uses the recipe 'Classic Lasagna'.", "Baking a cake uses the recipe 'Chocolate Fudge Cake'.", "Preparing dinner uses the recipe 'Chicken Stir-fry'."

candidates.label: permittedUsage
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the allowed uses or activities within an accommodation. Also called allowed uses, usage rules, permitted activities. Examples: An apartment has a permitted usage of 'Residential Only'. A hotel room has a permitted usage of 'Short-term Stay'. A conference hall has a permitted usage of 'Events and Meetings'.

candidates.label: potentialUse
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the intended use of a chemical substance or molecular entity by humans. Also called intended application, human use, purpose. Examples: A chemical substance has a potential use as 'fertilizer'. A molecular entity has a potential use as 'drug component'. The compound has a potential use in 'food preservation'.

candidates.label: educationalUse
candidates.comment: An educational use relation between a creative work or learning resource and its purpose in an educational context. Also called "learning purpose", "pedagogical use", "instructional application". Examples: "Worksheet educationalUse 'Assignment'", "Video educationalUse 'Group work'", "Simulation educationalUse 'Experiment'".

candidates.label: vehicleSpecialUsage
candidates.comment: A vehicle special usage relation between a vehicle and an indication of whether it has been used for special purposes like commercial rental or as a taxi. Also called special use, commercial use, past usage. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Taxi'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Commercial Rental'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Driving School'".

candidates.label: usageInfo
candidates.comment: A usage info relation between a creative work and additional information about its use, including licensing options, citation conventions, or purchasing details. Also called usage guidelines, licensing information, rights information. Examples: "CreativeWork usageInfo 'https://example.com/usage-policy'", "Image usageInfo 'Commercial licenses available upon request.'", "Dataset usageInfo 'https://example.com/data-license'". Distinct from license, which indicates the specific license(s) applicable to the content.

candidates.label: availableLanguage
candidates.comment: A language that can be used with or at an item, service, or place. Also called: supported language, language option, communication language. Examples: "ContactPoint 'Support' availableLanguage 'en'", "Course 'Programming' availableLanguage 'es'", "LodgingBusiness 'Hotel' availableLanguage 'fr'". Distinct from inLanguage, which specifies the language of the content itself.

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

chosen_property.label: struck
chosen_property.definition: The subject entity attacked or hit the object entity.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits this relation.

candidates.label: knownVehicleDamages
candidates.comment: A vehicle condition relation between a vehicle and a textual description of its known damages, whether repaired or not. Also called vehicle damage report, damage history, known defects, condition notes. Examples: A used car has knownVehicleDamages 'minor dent on rear bumper'. A vehicle has knownVehicleDamages 'repaired fender bender'. A truck has knownVehicleDamages 'scratches on passenger side door'. Distinct from vehicleCondition, which is a general assessment, not specific damages.

candidates.label: seriousAdverseOutcome
candidates.comment: A severe complication or side effect, such as death, disability, or life-threatening conditions, that may result from a medical device or therapy. Also called severe side effect, major complication, critical adverse event. Examples: `Chemotherapy` seriousAdverseOutcome `Severe Immunosuppression`, `Surgical Procedure` seriousAdverseOutcome `Infection`, `Medical Device Implant` seriousAdverseOutcome `Device Malfunction Leading to Injury`. Distinct from `adverseOutcome`, which is a more general adverse event.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: purchaseDate
candidates.comment: A purchase date relation between a product or vehicle and the date it was acquired by its current owner. Also called acquired on, bought on, ownership date. Examples: "A car has a purchase date of 2020-05-10.", "A smartphone has a purchase date of 2023-01-15.", "A house has a purchase date of 2018-07-22.". Distinct from productionDate, which is the date the item was manufactured.

candidates.label: ownedFrom
candidates.comment: The date and time when ownership of a product was obtained. Also called acquisition date, purchase date, date acquired. Examples: "Car OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2020-01-15'", "House OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2018-06-01T10:00:00'", "Book OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2023-03-10'". Distinct from ownedThrough, which is the date ownership ended.

candidates.label: associatedDisease
candidates.comment: A medical condition or URL representing a disease linked to a biochemical entity. Also called: related disease, disease connection, disease association. Examples: "BioChemEntity 'Insulin' associatedDisease 'Diabetes'", "BioChemEntity 'Gene X' associatedDisease 'Cancer'", "BioChemEntity 'Drug Y' associatedDisease 'Hypertension'."

candidates.label: workFeatured
candidates.comment: A featured work relation between an event and a creative work, indicating that the work is highlighted or showcased within the event. Also called showcased work, highlighted work, exhibited work. Examples: ExhibitionEvent workFeatured PaintingA, FestivalEvent workFeatured SculptureB, ConferenceEvent workFeatured ResearchPaperC. Distinct from workPerformed, which is a live rendition of a work, and workPresented, which is a specific presentation of a movie at a screening event.

candidates.label: sensoryUnit
candidates.comment: The neurological pathway or anatomical structure that transmits sensory information to the brain or spinal cord. Also called sensory pathway, afferent pathway, nerve input. Examples: `Optic Nerve` sensoryUnit `Retina`, `Auditory Nerve` sensoryUnit `Cochlea`, `Median Nerve` sensoryUnit `Skin of Hand`. Distinct from `motorUnit`, which transmits motor commands.

candidates.label: releaseOf
candidates.comment: A release of relation between a music release and the music album it originates from. Also called part of album, from album. Examples: "A music release 'Single A' is a release of 'Album X'.", "A digital track is a release of 'The Greatest Hits Album'.", "A vinyl edition is a release of 'Classic Rock Album'."

chosen_property.label: spokenByCharacter
chosen_property.justification: The 'spokenByCharacter' property from schema.org fits this relation.

candidates.label: spokenByCharacter
candidates.comment: An attribution relation between a quotation and the character, person, or organization to whom it is attributed within a creative work. Also called "attributed to", "quote speaker", "character says", "uttered by". Examples: "The quote is spokenByCharacter Hamlet", "The dialogue was spokenByCharacter the CEO", "This line is spokenByCharacter a fictional narrator."

candidates.label: slogan
candidates.comment: A memorable phrase or motto associated with a brand, organization, product, or service. Also called motto, tagline, catchphrase, jingle. Examples: `Brand: Nike` slogan `"Just Do It."`, `Organization: WWF` slogan `"For a living planet."`, `Product: Apple iPhone` slogan `"Think Different."`. Distinct from `name`, which is the official name.

candidates.label: founder
candidates.comment: A founder relation between an organization and the person or organization that established it. Also called: established by, created by, initiated by. Examples: "Microsoft" founder "Bill Gates", "Apple Inc." founder "Steve Jobs", "Google" founder "Larry Page". Distinct from founders, which is specifically for multiple people.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: hasOccupation
candidates.comment: An occupation relation between a person and their current occupation. Also called profession, job, employment. Examples: "A person has an occupation as a software engineer.", "She has an occupation as a doctor.", "His occupation is a teacher."

candidates.label: knows
candidates.comment: A general acquaintance relation between two people who are known to each other socially or professionally. Also called acquainted with, familiar with, knows personally, has met. Examples: John knows 'Jane'. Sarah knows 'her colleague Tom'. The CEO knows 'the board members'. Distinct from follows, friend, or memberOf, which imply more specific types of relationships.

candidates.label: owns
candidates.comment: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of. Examples: "John Doe owns 'a car'", "Acme Corp owns 'a patent'", "Sarah owns 'her house'". Distinct from memberOf, which describes membership in a group.

candidates.label: acceptedAnswer
candidates.comment: An accepted answer relation between a question and the answer(s) deemed best or most appropriate. Also called best answer, chosen solution, preferred response. Examples: "A forum question's accepted answer is 'Use a screwdriver'.", "A quiz question's accepted answer is 'Option B'."

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: owner
candidates.comment: A person or organization that owns a thing. Also called proprietor, possessor, title holder. Examples: "Car owner 'John Doe'", "Company owner 'Acme Corp'", "House owner 'Smith Family Trust'". Distinct from creator, who made the thing.

chosen_property.label: requested
chosen_property.definition: The subject entity made a request to the object entity.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits this relation.

candidates.label: seeks
candidates.comment: A demand for specific products or services expressed by an organization or person. Also called desires, looks for, requests, requires. Examples: `Company X` seeks `Demand for Software Developers`, `Person Y` seeks `Demand for Used Car`, `Organization Z` seeks `Demand for Consulting Services`. Distinct from `offers`, which is about what is provided.

candidates.label: rsvpResponse
candidates.comment: The specific response (e.g., Yes, No, Maybe) provided to an RSVP request. Also called RSVP status, attendance response, invitation reply. Examples: `Wedding RSVP` rsvpResponse `RsvpResponseType: Yes`, `Conference RSVP` rsvpResponse `RsvpResponseType: No`, `Party Invitation` rsvpResponse `RsvpResponseType: Maybe`.

candidates.label: permissions
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute detailing the permissions required for a software application to function. Also called access requirements, app permissions, authorization needs. Examples: A mobile app requires permissions for 'full internet access'. A software application requires permissions for 'access to camera'. A game requires permissions for 'storage access'.

candidates.label: requiresSubscription
candidates.comment: A subscription requirement relation indicating whether an action access or media object necessitates a subscription for use. Also called subscription needed, paywall, access restriction. Examples: "A streaming movie requires subscription 'true'.", "A news article requires subscription 'false'.", "A premium feature requires subscription 'true'."

candidates.label: eligibilityToWorkRequirement
candidates.comment: An eligibility to work requirement relation between a job posting and the text describing the legal documentation needed for an applicant. Also called "work authorization", "visa requirements", "employment eligibility". Examples: "Job posting eligibilityToWorkRequirement 'Must be authorized to work in the US'", "Job eligibilityToWorkRequirement 'Valid work permit required'", "Job eligibilityToWorkRequirement 'EU citizenship or valid visa'".

candidates.label: expectsAcceptanceOf
candidates.comment: An expects acceptance of relation between an action access specification, consume action, or media subscription and an offer that must be accepted before the action can be performed. Also called: requires offer, prerequisite offer, conditional offer. Examples: "Watch Movie Action" expects acceptance of "Movie Purchase Offer", "Download Software Action" expects acceptance of "Software License Offer", "Access Premium Content" expects acceptance of "Subscription Offer".

candidates.label: browserRequirements
candidates.comment: A description of browser requirements for a web application. Also called "browser compatibility", "required browser features". Examples: "Online banking app browserRequirements 'Requires Chrome 80+ or Firefox 75+'", "Video streaming service browserRequirements 'Supports HTML5 video and DRM'".

candidates.label: applicantLocationRequirements
candidates.comment: An applicant location requirements relation between a job posting and the administrative area(s) from which candidates can apply, especially for remote positions. Also called remote work location, eligible application region, telecommuting area. Examples: "A job posting's applicant location requirements include 'Anywhere in the US'.", "The remote job's applicant location requirements are 'Europe'."

candidates.label: offers
candidates.comment: An offer or demand related to a product, service, event, or other item. Also called available offers, related offers, product offers. Examples: "Product X offers 'Offer to sell'", "Service Y offers 'Demand for service'", "Event Z offers 'Offer for tickets'". Distinct from hasOfferCatalog, which points to a catalog of offers.

candidates.label: requiredGender
candidates.comment: A required gender relation between a people audience and the specific gender criteria for inclusion. Also called target gender, gender requirement. Examples: "An event targets a people audience with required gender 'female'.", "A survey specifies a required gender 'male'.", "A product is marketed to a people audience with required gender 'unspecified'."
